raw_response:
I'm 63 this year, been farming these 30 mu in Quzhou for 35 years. Only finished primary school, can't read those thick books, but I know this land. My legs ache in the morning now, and I can't lift what I used to, but my eyes still work — I can tell if wheat needs water just by the color.

Eight people in my household, but my older son works construction in Handan, only comes back for harvest. His wife stays with us and helps. My younger son is here but he does odd jobs in town when he can. So really it's me, my wife, my daughter-in-law, and my younger son who do the farm work. The grandchildren are in school.

I have 18 mu in wheat-maize, that's the main thing, been doing it 20 years. Eight mu in cotton on the lighter soil in the south of my land. And 4 mu of garlic I started five years ago when the price was good. My wife handles the garlic, she has the patience for it.

For the wheat on 18 mu: I'll plant around October 12th. Last year I used saved seed and got rust, so this year I'm buying new seed, the improved variety my neighbor Li uses. Costs about 30 yuan per mu, but better than losing yield. Before planting I'll rotavate the field — I hire a tractor, 40 yuan per mu, I don't have my own anymore. I put down base fertilizer: one bag of compound fertilizer per mu, that's 50 kg. Then at jointing, if the wheat looks a bit yellow, I topdress with half a bag of urea, about 25 kg. I irrigate three times: winter irrigation after New Year if it's dry, then at jointing in March, then at heading in April. Pumping costs money, electricity isn't cheap, but I won't skip it — I remember 1997 when the drought halved my wheat. I hire a combine for harvest in early June, 50 yuan per mu. I expect around 450 kg per mu if the year is normal.

The maize goes in right after wheat harvest, usually June 8-10. Only about a week to get it planted, sometimes I hire a planter tractor. I buy hybrid seed, about 3-4 jin per mu, costs around 40 yuan. I put compound fertilizer in the planting furrow, about 40 kg per mu. If rain is good I might not topdress, but usually I add some urea at the big trumpet stage, about 15 kg per mu. I irrigate once or twice — at big trumpet and maybe at filling if it's very dry. Harvest is late September, machine again. I expect 500 kg per mu.

Cotton on 8 mu: I plant around April 20th. Buy new seed every year, about 3 jin per mu. Put down base fertilizer, 40 kg compound per mu. Topdress at flowering with some urea. The big worry is insects — bollworm mostly. I spray four times, insecticide and some fungicide. Irrigate twice, at flowering and when the bolls are forming. Picking is hardest — we pick some ourselves, hire women from the village, pay by the kilo. Last year I got 250 kg per mu of seed cotton, hoping for 280 this year.

Garlic on 4 mu: We plant in mid-October, same time as wheat. We save our own cloves for seed, about 300 jin per mu — sounds like a lot but you need big cloves. I put down plenty of fertilizer: compound plus some chicken manure we got cheap from the chicken farm nearby. Then topdress in March when it greens up, and again in April. Water it four times. The main disease is white rot, so I spray fungicide twice. Harvest is late May, we dig it by hand — my wife and daughter-in-law do most of that, my back can't take the bending. If price is 3 yuan per jin, it's worth it. Last year it dropped to 2 yuan and I barely made money, but I'm keeping it because my wife likes having the cash crop.

Total costs this year: seed, fertilizer, pesticide, diesel for pumping, machine hire — probably around 18,000 yuan. I have some savings, and my older son sent 8,000 yuan last month. I don't borrow from the bank if I can help it. My neighbor Wang went to agricultural college, uses computers and all that, gets 100 kg more per mu than me. But I sleep fine. I've fed my family for 35 years doing it my way.
